title: Workspace settings profiles: Allow "Per-project themes" and more workspace specific settings

labels.name: cla-signed

body: Closes - #13300 Release Notes: - Added "Workspace Settings Profiles", which allows opening multiple Zed windows with different "Themes" and settings based on the project path ## Disclaimer Hi! Let's keep in mind that - This is my first contribution - Rust is not my most comfortable language I really tried my best but you know... hehe ANY criticism is super welcome!!! 🙂 I mean it Please read the last commit's title... which was the limit of my ability 😅 > WIP: HELP this was 100% vibecoded and I don't understand most of it That being said, it KINDA works! It's a solid Proof of Concept ## VIDEO SHOWCASE (🔉 sound on) I made this with much love and I think it's pretty good at explaining the UX and the current state of things - It's on YOUTUBE - It has 7 min and is too big for Github - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xDXLiVV8bhE --- ## Implementation Checklist ### Setup: Settings Schema & Resolution **[✅] Settings schema for `workspace_profiles`** Added `WorkspaceProfileSettingsContent` with `path` + `settings`, integrated into `UserSettingsContent`. Supports exact paths, tilde expansion, and glob patterns. ```json // settings.json { "workspace_profiles": { "foss": { "path": "~/projects/FOSS/*", "theme": "Dracula Solid" }, "timetravel": { "path": "~/projects/FOSS/timetravel", "theme": "Ayu Light" } }, } ``` **[✅] Path matching & precedence** `Workspace::match_path()` handles exact/glob matching. `Workspace::winning_workspace_profile()` picks the winner. Precedence: exact matches first, then glob matches (first wins in each tier). **[✅] Debug view** Created `workspace_profile_resolution.rs` with `OpenWorkspaceProfileResolution` action. Shows root paths, matched/unmatched profiles, and the winning profile. --- ### State Management: Window Context & Settings Resolution Here's where I am INSECURE! Very Proof of concept territory... I recommend reading what I did **[✅] Window context propagation (GPUI)** Thread-local `CURRENT_WINDOW_CONTEXT` tracks the rendering window. `Window::draw()` manages it automatically. Public `Window::current_window_id()` API exposes the context - I think of it like React Context for passing `windowId` down the tree 😅 . **[🤖 _vibecoded!_ ] Workspace profile → Settings cache** `SettingsStore` pre-computes `workspace_profile_settings: HashMap>` when settings change. Profile name is the cache key so multiple workspaces can share the same merged settings. **[🤖 _vibecoded!_ ] Settings indirection layer** `WorkspaceProfileMap` global maps `WindowId → Workspace Profile Name`. `Workspace::render()` registers itself. `GlobalTheme::theme(cx)` does the dance: get window ID from context → lookup profile name → return workspace theme from cache (or fallback to global). Works for all 1000+ `cx.theme()` calls with zero breaking changes. > Buuut, that being said, the name "Global" kinda feels weird now. I wouldn't expect "GlobalTheme::theme(cx)" to be the name of the thing that checks first for a "non global" theme.... although the way the workspace settings is being stored I guess is kinda global. **[⚠️] Hot reload support** Workspace themes recompute when `SettingsStore` changes via `observe_global`. Currently experiencing some inconsistency - themes don't always update properly on already-open windows. Probably a caching issue that needs investigation. Works fine on fresh window opens though!
